subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

learningObjectives.title: Atomic structure and the Periodic Table
Covalent, giant covalent and metallic bonding

questions.q: What is an element?
options: A substance made of only one type of atom
Two or more different elements chemically combined
Two or more substances that are not chemically combined
A metal dissolved in water
questions.explain: An element contains only one kind of atom and cannot be broken down into simpler substances by chemical means.

questions.q: What is a compound?
options: Two or more different elements chemically combined
Two or more elements simply mixed together
A substance made of only one type of atom
A solution of a salt in water
questions.explain: A compound is formed when different elements are chemically bonded together in fixed proportions.

questions.q: Why is clean, dry air classified as a mixture?
options: Its gases are not chemically combined and keep their own properties
Its gases are chemically bonded in a fixed ratio
It contains only one element
It can only be separated by a chemical reaction
questions.explain: In a mixture the components are not chemically joined, so they retain their own properties and can be separated physically.

questions.q: Which statement correctly distinguishes a compound from a mixture?
options: A compound has a fixed composition whereas a mixture does not
A mixture always has a fixed composition
A compound has the same properties as the elements in it
A mixture can only be separated by electrolysis
questions.explain: Compounds have a fixed ratio of elements and new properties, while mixtures vary in composition and keep their components' properties.

questions.q: What are the relative charges of a proton, a neutron and an electron respectively?
questions.explain: Protons carry a +1 charge, neutrons are neutral (0) and electrons carry a -1 charge.

questions.q: Which subatomic particle has a negligible (very small) relative mass?
options: Electron
Proton
Neutron
Nucleus
questions.explain: Protons and neutrons each have a relative mass of 1, while the electron's mass is negligible (about 1/2000).

questions.q: In a neutral atom, the number of electrons is equal to which quantity?
options: The number of protons
The number of neutrons
The number of protons plus neutrons
Twice the number of protons
questions.explain: A neutral atom has no overall charge, so its equal numbers of positive protons and negative electrons balance out.

questions.q: Chlorine has a proton number of 17. What is its electronic configuration?
questions.explain: Electrons fill shells 2 then 8 then 8; 17 electrons give 2,8,7 with seven in the outer shell.

questions.q: An element is in Group VII of the Periodic Table. How many electrons are in its outer shell?
questions.explain: The Group number equals the number of outer-shell electrons, so Group VII elements have seven.

questions.q: What does the period number of an element tell you about its atoms?
options: The number of occupied electron shells
The number of outer-shell electrons
The number of neutrons
The relative atomic mass
questions.explain: The period number gives the number of electron shells that contain electrons.

questions.q: Which statement correctly defines isotopes?
options: Atoms of the same element with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons
Atoms with the same number of neutrons but different numbers of protons
Atoms with different numbers of protons and electrons
Atoms with the same mass number but different proton numbers
questions.explain: Isotopes share the same proton number but differ in neutron number, giving different mass numbers.

questions.q: Why do isotopes of the same element have identical chemical properties?
options: They have the same electronic configuration
They have the same number of neutrons
They have the same mass number
They have different numbers of protons
questions.explain: Chemical behaviour depends on the electron arrangement, which is the same for all isotopes of an element.

questions.q: How many neutrons are present in an atom of chlorine-37 (proton number 17)?
questions.explain: Number of neutrons = mass number - proton number = 37 - 17 = 20.

questions.q: What is an ionic bond?
options: The strong electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions
A shared pair of electrons between two atoms
The attraction between metal ions and delocalised electrons
A weak force of attraction between molecules
questions.explain: Ionic bonding is the electrostatic attraction between positive and negative ions formed by electron transfer.

questions.q: When sodium reacts with chlorine to form sodium chloride, what happens to the electrons?
options: Sodium transfers an electron to chlorine
Sodium and chlorine share a pair of electrons
Chlorine transfers an electron to sodium
Both atoms lose electrons to each other
questions.explain: Sodium loses one electron to form Na+ and chlorine gains it to form Cl-, giving both full outer shells.

questions.q: Aluminium forms Al3+ ions and oxygen forms O2- ions. What is the formula of aluminium oxide?
options: Al2O3
AlO
Al3O2
AlO3
questions.explain: Balancing charges, two Al3+ (+6) combine with three O2- (-6) to give the neutral formula Al2O3.

questions.q: What is a covalent bond?
options: A shared pair of electrons between two atoms
A transfer of electrons from one atom to another
The electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions
A sea of delocalised electrons around metal ions
questions.explain: A covalent bond forms when two atoms share a pair of electrons to gain stable outer shells.

questions.q: Why do simple molecular substances have low melting and boiling points?
options: The weak forces between molecules are easily overcome
Strong covalent bonds between atoms are broken
Ionic bonds within the molecules are broken
Delocalised electrons are removed from the structure
questions.explain: Melting only breaks the weak intermolecular forces, not the strong covalent bonds, so little energy is needed.

questions.q: Why does graphite conduct electricity while diamond does not?
options: Graphite has delocalised electrons that are free to move
Diamond contains ions that carry charge
Graphite is actually a metal
Diamond has free electrons in its structure
questions.explain: In graphite each carbon bonds to three others, leaving one delocalised electron per atom free to carry charge; diamond's carbons all form four bonds.

questions.q: What is metallic bonding?
options: The attraction between positive metal ions and a sea of delocalised electrons
Shared pairs of electrons between metal atoms
The attraction between oppositely charged ions
Weak intermolecular forces between metal molecules
questions.explain: Metallic bonding is the electrostatic attraction between a lattice of positive metal ions and the delocalised outer electrons.

specSource: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry (0620) syllabus; Atoms, Elements & Compounds
